pr_title: docs: make all examples compatible with strict mode
pr_body:
Turns on the `strict` compiler flag and resolves the compilation errors in the various AIO examples.

Closes #42107
pr_comments: Regarding the non-null assertions: that's actually what I prefer as well, but there's a lint rule that doesn't allow them. I believe it's one that is turned on by default in the CLI.

> Regarding the non-null assertions: that's actually what I prefer as well, but there's a lint rule that doesn't allow them. I believe it's one that is turned on by default in the CLI.

What 😱 ??? That is a bad lint rule.

Since tslint is deprecated in v12, we should not be using it for our examples anyway :-)

So I would recommend deleting the `tslint.json` file from the boillerplate and removing the lint rule from the `angular.json`. See https://github.com/cexbrayat/angular-cli-diff/compare/11.2.9..12.0.0-rc.2#diff-35cddbe68960b288daa0aeb84cc609451029d160e3524e0d3ad17061cc20eeaeL99

I agree on disabling the rule, but do we really want to disable linting completely on the examples? We could have a follow-up task to switch AIO to Eslint, like we did recently for the Material docs: https://github.com/angular/material.angular.io/pull/957

> I agree on disabling the rule, but do we really want to disable linting completely on the examples? We could have a follow-up task to switch AIO to Eslint, like we did recently for the Material docs: [angular/material.angular.io#957](https://github.com/angular/material.angular.io/pull/957)

Yes to disabling that rule. And yes to a follow up PR to replace tslint with eslint.

Happy to approve this as it is, to get it done before 12.0.0 gets too much attention.
We can iterate on small disagreements on style in follow up PRs.
@crisbeto it looks like this PR has all the necessary approvals now :)

review_comments: What was wrong with `this.resend()`?
The TS check for strict initialization wouldn't pick up that `message$` was initialized. I think that this is cleaner as well.

Hmm, I left a comment on this yesterday but it got lost somehow 🤔. The reason I changed `questions` to `| null` is because the example passes them in with an `async` pipe in one of the templates. The `async` pipe starts off with a `null` value.
In which case we should not be casting it to `QuestionBase<string>[]` on line 22, right?
Why is the `| null` part needed? 😕
FWIW, I find it strange that we use `!` for some inputs and initial values for others 🤷‍♂️
It's just that some properties are easier to initialize than others.
Good call
This looks a bit confusing (though correct). Could you plz add a quick comment here (why we do non-null asserting for the  `null` value)?

I would rather cast this to `as unknown as Console` that spy on `console.log` 😱
(This would also be more consistent with casting to `Document` below.)
I'm not a fan of constructing these object literals all over the place, but I can try to replace them with `jasmine.createSpyObj`.
Same as above: I'd rather avoid spying on `console.log`.
@crisbeto just curious if this field was unused?
As far as I could tell, it wasn't being used.

In general, I am not sure that moving these calls (here and in other examples) from `ngOnInit()` to the constructor is a change we want to show. It doesn't make a difference here, but in a real-word app, we recommend making such calls (that typically make HTTP requests) in `ngOnInit()`.
Why not `number`?
There's this issue where the browser typings return `number`, but Node returns `Timer` and it causes vscode to complain.
OOC, why is this change needed?
I think it was due to strict null checks.
ASIDE: we should rename this to `Boss` or similar. Something for another PR, since that would also involve changes to the guide and associated screenshots.

I kept it, because it's referenced in the view and I wasn't sure whether it isn't trying to illustrate something in a tutorial.
